facts.narrative: 71-year-old male on dialysis three times a week. During the February 2021 winter storm, the dialysis center closed and roads were solid ice, preventing him from attending sessions starting February 15. He became very short of breath and died at home on February 19, 2021. Death certificate lists cardiac arrest as cause.

# DRAFT: Certifier statement on disaster relationship

> **Draft prepared by Counted for review. Not a death certificate. Not valid until reviewed and signed by the
> certifying medical examiner, coroner or physician.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Case | d169ba053114 |
| Decedent | age 71, male |
| Date of death | 2021-02-19 |
| Location | Travis County, TX |
| Disaster | February 2021 winter storm (DR-4586-TX); incident period 2021-02-11 to 2021-02-21 |
| NWS warnings in force | Winter Storm Warning (2021-02-13), Wind Chill Warning (2021-02-15), Wind Chill Advisory (2021-02-15), Hard Freeze Warning (2021-02-16), Wind Chill Warning (2021-02-16) |
| Cause on certificate (per family) | cardiac arrest |

## Determination (CDC 2017 Reference Guide)
In my opinion this death was **indirectly caused** by February 2021 winter storm (DR-4586-TX).

**Causal chain:** The February 2021 winter storm (DR-4586-TX) caused road closures due to solid ice and closure of the dialysis center, preventing a 71-year-old male with end-stage renal disease from attending dialysis sessions beginning February 15; missed dialysis led to fluid and metabolic derangement, respiratory distress, and cardiac arrest, resulting in death at home on February 19, 2021.

**Proposed "How injury occurred" (Item 43):** Dialysis center closed and roads rendered impassable by ice during the February 2021 winter storm (DR-4586-TX), causing the decedent to miss multiple hemodialysis sessions beginning February 15, 2021; resultant fluid overload and metabolic derangement precipitated respiratory distress and fatal cardiac arrest at home on February 19, 2021.

**Proposed wording for FEMA Funeral Assistance** (FEMA rejects "may have been caused by"):
> This death was indirectly caused by February 2021 winter storm (DR-4586-TX).

## Family account (verbatim)
- "The center closed during the February 2021 winter storm and the roads were solid ice, so he missed his sessions from February 15." (loss of health care)
- "He became very short of breath and died at home on 2021-02-19." (exacerbation of chronic illness)

# Funeral Assistance: what to gather

We are very sorry for your loss. FEMA may help with funeral costs when a death was caused directly or indirectly by a declared disaster.

Good news: FEMA Individual Assistance was approved for Travis County under DR-4586-TX. Funeral Assistance is part of that program.

- [ ] Death certificate, OR the signed certifier statement Counted drafted (ask the medical examiner or doctor to review and sign it)
- [ ] Funeral home contract or itemized receipts
- [ ] Proof of any other help received (insurance, burial societies, donations)
- [ ] The decedent's and applicant's names and addresses

Apply at DisasterAssistance.gov or call 1-800-621-3362. If FEMA says no, you can appeal in writing using the appeal letter below.

## Appeal letter (fill in and sign)

> I am appealing FEMA's decision on Funeral Assistance for __________, who died on 2021-02-19 in Travis County. The enclosed statement from the certifier states the death was indirectly caused by February 2021 winter storm (DR-4586-TX): The February 2021 winter storm (DR-4586-TX) caused road closures due to solid ice and closure of the dialysis center, preventing a 71-year-old male with end-stage renal disease from attending dialysis sessions beginning February 15; missed dialysis led to fluid and metabolic derangement, respiratory distress, and cardiac arrest, resulting in death at home on February 19, 2021.. I ask FEMA to reconsider.

_Counted cannot promise any outcome. FEMA makes the decision._
